data.narrative:
Perennial Autonomy operates in Defense & Security at the government-contract stage, backed by Schmidt-family capital and a $500M IDIQ award. The sector encompasses 21 peer companies, of which 2 trade publicly (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 are private, including notable players such as Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems.

Peer-median valuation proved inapplicable due to insufficient comparable datapoints. While 21 same-sector peers exist, filtering for matching stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints—the minimum threshold for reliable triangulation. Restricting analysis to all-sector medians would introduce material bias given the heterogeneity of Defense & Security valuations across earlier and later-stage companies.

The absence of tight-fit comparables reflects the nascent and specialized nature of Perennial Autonomy's position: government-contract-stage frontier technology with founder-level backing in a sector that rarely produces same-stage, same-scale peer transactions. Any valuation framework must therefore rely heavily on non-quantitative factors—contract terms, IDIQ scope, team composition, and capital deployment trajectory—rather than market multiples. Key uncertainties include contract execution velocity, competitive positioning within the identified peer set, and the sustainability of government funding. Further analysis requires either closer comparables or a cash-flow-based methodology anchored to IDIQ terms.
